ledgers.artifact: Alexandria — The Library That Cannot Burn
ledgers.diamond_cut_verdict: Not yet diamond-cut. Conceptually strong and coherent, but it carries two spine-level self-contradictions that undercut its own honesty thesis: (1) you click "burn the center" and the canvas prints "the center is gone," while the center's own prose insists it is "the only room the fire cannot touch"; (2) the always-on thesis asserts present-tense "every navigator carries a pocket Alexandria (local-first vault)" while the SELF-SOVEREIGNTY hall honestly grades that exact vault as c-gap/plan — an ADR-044 temporal-provenance leak. Add a dead payoff animation (re-seed drives burnT but draw() never reads it when burned===false, so the thesis gesture is a hard snap), a stale count in the hall literally named for traceability ("32 ADRs" vs 44 files), and two genuine WCAG small-text failures. Clarity 66/100.

confirmed.claim: The core interaction burns 'the center' and declares it gone, while the center's own prose insists the fire cannot touch it — a direct self-contradiction on click.
confirmed.evidence: Button line 47 'burn the center'; burned canvas caption line 160 'the center is gone' under 'THE FIRE' (line 158). Yet center drawer heading line 211 'The only room the fire cannot touch' and def line 93 '...the only room the fire test cannot touch, because it was never stored here.' The thing you click to burn is the same room the copy calls unburnable — the demo refutes its own thesis.
confirmed.fix: Separate the two 'centers' the metaphor conflates: the singular vault that SHOULD burn vs. the om that can't. Either relabel the button 'burn the archive' and keep the center serene (drop 'the center is gone'), or drop the 'cannot touch' claim.

confirmed.claim: The always-visible thesis states the local-first vault as present fact, but the artifact's own SELF-SOVEREIGNTY hall grades that vault as not-built (c-gap/plan) — an ADR-044 temporal-provenance violation.
confirmed.evidence: HUD line 55 (permanently on screen): 'every navigator carries a pocket Alexandria (local-first vault)' — present tense. But line 78 grades 'L3 local vault' and 'L4 GIGI substrate' both c-gap, and line 79 shelves them as 'plan' (not real). Center drawer line 213 doubles down present-tense: 'Every navigator's vault is a full library in miniature.' The fine-print ladder (line 214) already discloses the honest sequencing; the headline contradicts it.
confirmed.fix: Tense-hedge the thesis to match the halls: 'every navigator will carry a pocket Alexandria (L3/L4 — planned)' or 'the design carries the vault to the edges.' Make the headline honor line 214 instead of contradicting it.

confirmed.claim: All substantive content (halls' laws, chips, scroll census, center reading-room text) is reachable ONLY by mouse-clicking canvas wedges — no keyboard path, no text alternative.
confirmed.evidence: Line 52 <canvas id="cv"> has no role/aria-label/fallback. All content injected on cv click (line 182) → openHall/openCenter (lines 193, 207). Only keyboard-reachable controls are the deck buttons + ESC (line 219); nothing focuses or opens a hall/center. A screen reader hits an empty canvas.
confirmed.fix: Add a visually-hidden but focusable list of the 5 halls + center mirroring the drawer content (real <button>s calling openHall). Give the canvas role="img" + aria-label summarizing the thesis. Move focus into the drawer on open, restore on close.

confirmed.claim: The re-seed gesture — the thesis payoff, 'burn any center and the library re-seeds from its edges' — has no animation at all; it is a hard cut.
confirmed.evidence: ignite(false) sets burned=false, burnT=0, then a rAF ramps burnT 0→1. But every burnT use in draw() is gated behind burned: scroll state is `burned ? ... : s[1]` (line 124), the ash tick + ember stub only exist when state==='ash' (burned only), and the center gradient is `if(burned){...burnT...}else{static}` (lines 148-152). With burned=false, draw() output is byte-identical for burnT=0 and burnT=1 — the ramp spins doing nothing while the scene snaps restored on frame 1.
confirmed.fix: Give re-seed its own read: drive an inbound sweep off burnT when burned===false (sov ticks brighten/rise from the outer ring inward, ash fading up) so the ascending phrase has a visual counterpart.

confirmed.claim: The TRACEABILITY hall asserts '32 ADRs' as a sovereign count, but the repo has 44 ADR files (40 distinct numbers) — stale in the hall literally named for walking artifacts back to source. (Dedup: also raised by curator + skeptic on the same line.)
confirmed.evidence: Line 69 ['32 ADRs','sov']. Verified live: `ls _DECISIONS/ADR-*.md | wc -l` = 44; distinct ADR-NNN = 40; _DECISIONS/index.json lists 34. Every denominator exceeds 32. The '32' traces to a stale lattice JSON, not to source truth.
confirmed.fix: Update to the live count (44 files / 40 numbers / 34 per index — pick a canonical denominator and label it), or drop the number ('the ADR ledger') so it cannot drift again. Refresh the lattice SSOT it mirrors so the two agree.

confirmed.claim: Section-label eyebrows (.lbl) and the center-drawer footnote render in --mut (#475569), below the 4.5:1 AA floor for their small size.
confirmed.evidence: Line 12 .lbl{color:var(--mut)} at .6rem, used un-recolored for 'state of the hall' (line 201) and 'shelved scroll-lines' (line 203). Line 214 footnote color:var(--mut) at .75rem. Recomputed: #475569 on #020408 = 2.73:1; on drawer #0d1117 = 2.54:1. Both fail AA.
confirmed.fix: Raise these to at least --sec (#94a3b8 ≈ 7.4:1 on the drawer) or lighten --mut for text use; reserve #475569 for hairline strokes, never label/body copy.

confirmed.claim: The performance runs on two unsynced clocks — the burn animates in frame counts while the nocturne score fires on wall-clock timers — so sound and motion desync, worse on high-refresh displays.
confirmed.evidence: Visual burn advances `burnT + .02` per requestAnimationFrame (line 175) → ~833ms at 60Hz, ~415ms at 120Hz. The nocturne schedules on wall-clock: setTimeout(ignite,250/4400) (lines 244-245) and AudioContext onsets t0+i*.55 / t0+4.2+i*.45 (lines 242-243). The visual burn is static by ~1s while the scored fire phrase runs ~+0.2→3.8s; on a 120Hz Mac the visual finishes in half the time, sliding further apart.
confirmed.fix: Drive burnT from elapsed wall-clock (performance.now() delta / fixed duration), not a per-frame increment, and set that duration to match the scored phrase so sound and motion are one gesture on one clock, refresh-rate independent.

confirmed.claim: The NOCTURNE is decorative — a 27-line WebAudio subsystem plus a third deck button that only replays the fire+re-seed 'sung,' carrying no information the fire test doesn't already carry.
confirmed.evidence: Line 49 button ('🎼 nocturne') + lines 221-247 (oscillators, nPluck, two note phrases, nocTimers) do nothing but call the already-bound ignite(true)/ignite(false) on timers (lines 244-245). WORLD.md register: Myst 'didn't celebrate with confetti.'
confirmed.fix: Consider cutting the nocturne (delete line 49 + lines 221-247), leaving two honest controls: burn / re-seed. Biggest single subtraction available (~11% of the file + the third competing button). Judgment call — it is an alternate sensory channel, not strictly redundant.

confirmed.claim: The bottom-left HUD is an over-dense text-wall that re-teaches the color taxonomy the census line already encodes, and visually collides with the lower-left canvas hall label (INTEROPERABILITY).
confirmed.evidence: HUD is three long lines: line 55 thesis (~55 words) + line 56 legend/instructions + line 57 census. Line 56 spells out green=sovereign / ember=burn / steel=planned, which the census (line 166: '14 sovereign · 5 single-copy · 4 planned', verified) already encodes. INTEROPERABILITY is hall index 3, drawn down-left (hallAngle → ~126°) near the fixed HUD box, so overlap is likely.
confirmed.fix: Cut the color-glossary half of line 56; keep one instruction line ('click a hall · click the center'). Fewer HUD lines resolves both the redundancy and the label overlap. (Overlap inferred from geometry, not a fresh render — confirm with a screenshot.)

confirmed.claim: The visually dramatic part of 'burn the center' is a hard cut on frame 1; only a faint opacity tail is actually animated.
confirmed.evidence: On ignite(true), frame 1 already has burned=true, so burnable scrolls flip to state 'ash' immediately (line 124) and the tick color jumps from ember rgba(255,107,53,.7) (line 132) to slate rgba(71,85,105,.5) (line 129) in one frame. The 50-frame ramp only animates that slate dimming .5→.25 plus a 2px ember stub after burnT>.5 (line 134) — the eye-catching ember→ash change is instantaneous.
confirmed.fix: Interpolate the ember→ash color across burnT (lerp ember toward slate) instead of switching state on frame 1, so the consuming is what animates rather than a post-hoc dim.

confirmed.claim: The DE/COMPOSABILITY chip '22 atoms' over-counts and is the one number that doesn't match source, while the molecules/organisms counts beside it match exactly. (Dedup: skeptic raised the same line.)
confirmed.evidence: Line 88 ['22 atoms · 16 molecules · 5 organisms','c-ok']. Verified: src/molecules = 16 .tsx (match), src/organisms = 5 .tsx (match), but src/ui = 20 .tsx (two of which — PointerTypeProbe.tsx, ToastDrawerContext.tsx — are a probe and a context, not atoms) + tokens.ts + useVw.ts = 22 files. No reading yields 22 atoms; real atoms ≈18. The scroll-line even hedges 'src/ui atoms + tokens' (line 89).
confirmed.fix: State the honest figure ('18 atoms', or '22 src/ui files' if counting the module + hook deliberately) so the one number nobody checked stops being the outlier next to two exact ones.

confirmed.claim: The HUD instruction/census lines (.kv, ~10px) use --dim (#64748b), just under the 4.5:1 AA threshold for small text.
confirmed.evidence: Line 25 .kv{font-size:.62rem;color:var(--dim)} over the #020408 canvas fill. Recomputed #64748b on #020408 ≈ 4.37:1 — under 4.5:1. This is the primary orientation copy that teaches the whole interaction.
confirmed.fix: Bump .kv to --sec (#94a3b8) or nudge --dim up one step so the load-bearing legend clears 4.5:1.

confirmed.claim: Dead code in the per-frame render loop: scroll-line label coordinates are computed then explicitly discarded, rendering nothing.
confirmed.evidence: Lines 137-139: '// scroll-line label' comment then `const lx = CX + Math.cos(mid)*rr, ly = ...; void lx; void ly;` — draws no label. Runs 15×/frame (3 scrolls × 5 halls).
confirmed.fix: Delete lines 137-139 and the stale comment. Pure subtraction — vestige of an abandoned label feature.

confirmed.claim: 'the fire test is a design review, not a metaphor' overclaims rigor — the census is a hand-authored array of 23 lines, and the survive/lost figures merely tally that array.
confirmed.evidence: Line 166: 'the fire test is a design review, not a metaphor.' But sov/burn/plan are computed (lines 162-163) by iterating the hardcoded HALLS scroll list; every classification is a designer's judgment typed into lines 69-89, not an automated audit. Insisting it is 'not a metaphor' is the register-leak the Myst world forbids — a page telling the viewer how rigorous to find it.
confirmed.fix: Cut 'not a metaphor.' Let the census stand as what it is — an honest hand-graded design review. The insistence is what makes it read as sold-to.

confirmed.claim: A single linear ramp serves both gestures, so no easing distinguishes collapse from rise.
confirmed.evidence: `burnT = Math.min(1, burnT + .02)` (line 175) is the only easing in the file, reused verbatim for fire and re-seed. Per conductor-notation, a collapse reads decresc + luftpause and a rise reads accel/Élevé; a flat linear increment honors neither. (Note: partly subsumed by the fact that re-seed reads burnT nowhere — see the re-seed finding — so the 'rise' currently has no motion to ease at all.)
confirmed.fix: Once re-seed actually reads burnT, ease the two gestures differently — fire as an accelerating consume (ease-in + brief settle), re-seed as an ease-out rise.

confirmed.claim: The GIGI/pocket-Alexandria thesis is stated twice, and 'om' is used before it is glossed.
confirmed.evidence: HUD line 55 ('every navigator carries a pocket Alexandria… the network is the inter-library loan') is restated in the center drawer line 213 ('GIGI is not a bigger Alexandria… Every navigator's vault is a full library in miniature'). 'om' appears on line 56 and line 160 before its only gloss, which lives inside the center def (line 93/212, 'The om the library grows from').
confirmed.fix: Let the drawer own the full GIGI framing; trim the HUD thesis to its first sentence. Gloss 'om' once up front or replace with a plainer word.

confirmed.claim: The drawer close button .x has no focus-visible style and focus is never managed, so the drawer's only control has no visible keyboard affordance.
confirmed.evidence: Line 33 .x{...} defines no :focus-visible; the outline rule at line 21 is scoped to .btn only. Drawer open (lines 205/215) does not move focus; close (line 217) does not restore it.
confirmed.fix: Add .x:focus-visible{outline:1px solid var(--cyan)} and, when wiring keyboard access for the halls, move focus to .x on open and back to the trigger on close.

confirmed.claim: The burned-state enumeration names four categories for five counted losses.
confirmed.evidence: Line 165: '${burn} lost — user receipts, sage traces, machine-local memory, unreconciled tokens' renders '5 lost' (burn tally = 5, verified across the HALLS array) but lists 4 nouns; 'user receipts' is double-counted across the trace hall (line 69) and sov hall (line 79), so the prose silently collapses the fifth item.
confirmed.fix: Make the noun list five items, or reword to 'across receipts, traces, machine-local memory, and tokens' so the count and the enumeration stop disagreeing.

ledgers.diamond_cut_verdict: Not yet diamond-cut. The mark itself is coherent and on-register — the additive two-family interference, the buried-then-earned gold horizon, and the GRAIN speckle all read as one instrument. But it is not distilled: a control (Phase) is dead in the shipped default state, a promised invariant ("one conductor at a time") is half-wired, there is no viewport meta, tempo is authored to the refresh rate rather than to time, and two caption lines overclaim against ARCS's own doctrine ("earned, not granted" on a plain slider; naming itself the PARADOX/MOIRE state while not rendering at that degraded fidelity). Clarity ≈ 70/100.

confirmed.claim: The Phase slider is a dead control in the shipped default state — drift is on by default and loop() overwrites both S.phase and the slider's value every frame, so dragging it does nothing that survives one frame.
confirmed.evidence: Line 144 sets S.drift=true when !reduced and line 204 starts loop(); loop() (line 139) does `S.phase += .0035; document.getElementById('phase').value = Math.round((S.phase*100)%628)` every frame, and the input handler (line 132) only calls draw() `if (!S.drift)`. So in the default (drift-on) experience the Phase thumb is snapped back each frame and the drag has no lasting effect — a control that looks interactive but isn't. Confirmed against the bytes.
confirmed.fix: Delete the Phase slider (line 37) and its bind (line 136); drift already owns rotation and a manual scrubber is incoherent while it runs. If a manual scrub is wanted, have it pause drift on interaction instead of being silently overwritten.

confirmed.claim: The 'one conductor at a time' rule is only half-wired: starting drift while lune is playing leaves BOTH rAF loops alive, so two loops drive the same stage and double-advance S.phase.
confirmed.evidence: Line 188 (lune start) stops drift: `if (S.drift) document.getElementById('drift').click();`. But the drift handler (lines 140-143) has no reciprocal guard — it never checks LAC or stops lune. With lune playing, clicking drift sets S.drift=true and calls loop() while step() (line 191-200) still runs; both call draw() and both add to S.phase, so phase advances at ~loop+step tempo. (The 'fog flicker' sub-claim is weaker — loop() never touches S.fog, so fog stays lune-driven; the double-phase / double-draw is the solid defect.) The asymmetry is real in the file.
confirmed.fix: Make the guard symmetric: at the top of the drift click handler, if LAC is live, close/stop lune first (mirror line 188). Exactly one draw loop ever alive.

confirmed.claim: No viewport meta tag, so the full-viewport canvas + 6-item control deck render at desktop width on mobile.
confirmed.evidence: File head is line 1 `<meta charset="utf-8">`, line 2 `<title>`, then `<style>` — no `name="viewport"` anywhere. Layout depends on `width:100vw;height:100vh` (line 23), devicePixelRatio (line 50), and a flex deck of four 104px sliders + two buttons (lines 34-39). As a local-first _ARTIFACTS file opened directly, mobile will lay this out at ~980px and shrink it.
confirmed.fix: Add `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` at the top. (Moot only if this is always served through a publish skeleton that injects one — verify before dismissing.)

confirmed.claim: Rotation is authored to the viewer's refresh rate, not to time — phase advances a fixed amount per frame, so the strip spins ~2x faster at 120Hz and, in lune mode, desyncs from the time-based audio/fog.
confirmed.evidence: Line 139 `S.phase += .0035;` and line 196 `S.phase += .0022 + .0065 * e;` are per-frame with no delta-time. The same lune loop derives fog from real time (line 192 `raw = LAC.currentTime - luneT0`) and audio is scheduled in absolute AudioContext seconds (lines 169-172). So on a high-refresh panel the strip out-runs the score it is meant to dance to; tempo is incidental, not conducted.
confirmed.fix: Drive phase from elapsed time: capture performance.now() (or LAC.currentTime in lune) and scale the increment by dt/16.7 so one authored tempo holds across 60/120/144Hz and stays locked to the audio.

confirmed.claim: The LUNE / Clair de Lune subsystem is the single largest subtraction candidate — a full Debussy pluck-synth (~a quarter of the JS) bolted to a brand mark.
confirmed.evidence: Lines 146-201: 20-event LSCORE, dual-oscillator lPluck, lSched/lEnv, and the 🌙 button (line 39). It exists as claimed. The 'entirely off-thesis' framing is partly overstated — the comment's intent (fog parts as the melody swells = clarity earned by an external temporal signal, lines 146-147) does gesture at the earned-clarity thesis — but Debussy specifically carries no ARCS/PARADOX connection, and this is the clearest 'author-cosmology-over-guest' candidate WORLD.md warns against.
confirmed.fix: Consider cutting the lune subsystem wholesale (button, LSCORE, lPluck, lSched, lEnv, step-loop); Fog is already a first-class slider. If kept, it must earn its quarter of the payload — which the fidelity/floor defects below argue it does not yet.

confirmed.claim: The doctrine line 'Lower the fog and it is earned, not granted' is contradicted by the interaction: manual fog is a plain drag-slider that grants full clarity in one gesture.
confirmed.evidence: Caption line 44 vs line 36 `<input id="fog" type=range>` wired at line 135 `bind('fog', v => S.fog = v/100)`. Dragging to 0 grants full clarity instantly — the literal definition of 'granted.' Nothing gates or accrues the reveal on the manual path.
confirmed.fix: Cut 'earned, not granted' from the manual-fog caption (let the lune path, which at least ramps, carry the 'earned' claim), or gate the slider so clarity accrues rather than being draggable to zero.

confirmed.claim: The caption body copy — the load-bearing MOIRE / Möbius / horizon explanation — fails the 4.5:1 small-text contrast floor.
confirmed.evidence: `.cap .kv{...color:var(--dim)}` = #64748b at .62rem (~10px) over --bg #020408 (lines 25, 5). Recomputed WCAG ratio = 4.31:1 (L_text 0.1705, L_bg 0.00117), under the 4.5:1 floor for text below 18px. (Finding's 4.27 estimate is close.)
confirmed.fix: Raise `.kv` to `--sec` #94a3b8 (~7:1); reserve --dim for the italic quote only if a degraded accent is wanted.

confirmed.claim: The Fog slider's own text label is effectively illegible, failing even the 3:1 large-text floor.
confirmed.evidence: `.lbl{...color:var(--mut)}` = #475569 over #020408, `Fog` (line 36). Recomputed ratio = 2.71:1 (L 0.0885). Strands/Δ/Phase escape via .lbl.cy/.lbl.gd (lines 34,35,37); only Fog is bare --mut. At .6rem bold it isn't even 'large text', so the real floor is 4.5:1 — it fails either way.
confirmed.fix: Give Fog a colored variant like the other three, or bump `.lbl` base to at least #94a3b8 so the control's own name is readable.

confirmed.claim: The lune fog-breathing is a re-modeled proxy, not the signal the ear hears: a flat 1.1s decay ignores each note's real duration and snaps at the loop seam.
confirmed.evidence: lEnv (line 182) sums `ev[3]*Math.exp(-d/1.1)` — a hard-coded 1.1s decay for every note — while audio decays over each note's own `dur = ev[2]*LU*1.5` (up to 14*0.46*1.5 ≈ 9.7s for the ev[2]=14 bass, line 158/177). So the bass rings for seconds in the ear but is gone from the fog in ~1s. And `d = ts - ev[0]*LU` (line 182) goes negative when ts wraps at LLOOP*LU (line 192), so trailing notes drop out abruptly at the seam while the audio tails ring across it — a once-per-loop fog snap.
confirmed.fix: Feed the real signal: read RMS from an AnalyserNode on the lune output and map that to fog. That also erases the seam, since an analyser has no loop model to reset.

confirmed.claim: 'the pattern you see belongs to neither' is false at the Δ slider's own zero end, where the gold family exactly coincides with the cyan.
confirmed.evidence: Caption line 43. Both families walk the identical strand set `s/(N-1)` (lines 102 & 106), offset only by S.delta (bind line 134, default .022 rad). The Δ slider is `min="0"` (line 35), so at Δ=0 the gold family coincides with cyan — zero interference, and the pattern belongs to both, not neither. The 'faint at default' sub-claim is hedged/subjective, but the Δ=0 collapse is exact.
confirmed.fix: Raise the Δ floor above 0 (e.g. min=4) so an interference pattern always exists whenever the 'belongs to neither' claim is on screen.

confirmed.claim: The piece names itself the PARADOX / MOIRE render state yet does not apply the MOIRE degradation WORLD.md mandates for that state.
confirmed.evidence: Caption line 43 'MOIRE · the PARADOX render state.' WORLD.md's render scale requires MOIRE at opacity 0.60, weight 300, tracking +0.03em + a ::after overlay. The caption .kv sets no weight, no opacity, no ::after (line 25). WORLD.md does scope this to 'the brief and all UI sections,' so a UI caption is arguably in scope. Weaker point: the copy is already dimmed via color:var(--dim), so 'renders at full SHARP fidelity' overstates it — it's dim but not MOIRE-degraded.
confirmed.fix: If it declares itself PARADOX/MOIRE, apply the degradation to at least the label span; otherwise drop the 'render state' claim and let it be a brand mark.

confirmed.claim: 'the horizon is earned by ear' over-promises — the lune path floors fog at 0.08 and can never fully clear it.
confirmed.evidence: Comment line 147 'the horizon is earned by ear'; line 194 `S.fog = Math.max(.08, .9 - .85 * e)`. At peak envelope e≈1, .9-.85=.05, clamped up to .08 — a permanent haze. Only the hand-slider (line 135) reaches 0. Clarity is reachable by hand but not by ear.
confirmed.fix: Either let the envelope drive fog to 0 at the swell peak, or soften the comment to 'the horizon parts by ear' rather than 'earned.'

confirmed.claim: The prefers-reduced-motion CSS rule is dead code — it disables transitions on a page that has none.
confirmed.evidence: Line 27 `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){*{transition:none!important}}`. There are zero `transition:` declarations in the stylesheet; all motion is canvas rAF (loop/step). The real, correct gate is JS line 144 `if (!reduced)` suppressing auto-drift. Separately, the lune step-loop has no reduced-motion consideration once clicked.
confirmed.fix: Delete the no-op CSS rule. Optionally, under `reduced`, have lune advance in discrete steps or skip the phase spin so an opted-in viewer still gets audio without continuous rotation.

confirmed.claim: The canvas — the entire visual payload — exposes no text alternative or role to assistive tech.
confirmed.evidence: Line 30 `<canvas id="cv"></canvas>` has no aria-label, no role, no fallback child. The descriptive `.cap` is a sibling with pointer-events:none (line 24), not programmatically associated with the canvas.
confirmed.fix: Add role="img" and an aria-label naming the mark (e.g. 'ARCS Möbius brand mark: interfering strand families over a fog field with the gold True-North horizon').

confirmed.claim: Two micro-redundancies: an imperceptible terrain tint, and the caption says 'earned' twice in adjacent clauses.
confirmed.evidence: Line 94 `ctx.fillStyle='rgba(125,211,252,.05)'` fills below the horizon at 5% alpha, then gets buried under the fog gradients (lines 112-118) and the 88%-alpha vignette (line 127) — largely invisible ('renders nothing' is slightly overstated: at fog=0 the 5% tint is faintly present). Line 44 pairs 'it is earned, not granted' with the italic tagline 'earned clarity' — 'earned' stated twice back to back (this half is exact).
confirmed.fix: Delete line 94 (no visible signal). In the caption, keep one 'earned' beat — the plain sentence or the tagline quote, not both.
